programme.title: A Hard Day's Night
programme.desc: The Beatles in their feature film debut, one of the greatest rock-and-roll comedy adventures ever. The film has a fully restored negative and digitally restored soundtrack. The film takes on the just-left-of-reality style of mock-documentary, following "a day in the life" of John, Paul, George, and Ringo as fame takes them by storm. (Musical comedy) - 1964

programme.title: The Daytrippers
programme.desc: Eliza D'Amico's seemingly idyllic marriage to Louis changes dramatically when she discovers what she believes to be a love letter to him from someone else. Going home to her family for comfort, Eliza sets out with her mother, father, sister and her sister's boyfriend in the family car to track down and confront Louis. Always one step behind him, the family learns a lot about each other in the process. (Comedy) - 1996

programme.title: Mississippi Masala
programme.desc: After Mina's Indian family is ousted from their home in Uganda by dictator Idi Amin, they relocate to Mississippi to start a new life. Mina falls for Demetrius, a young carpet cleaner, despite the protestations of their families over their racial difference. The families and their surrounding communities begin to feud, putting even more pressure on the couple's romance. Having to choose between family and love, Mina and Demetrius run away together. (Comedy drama) - 1991

programme.title: Hall Pass
programme.desc: Best friends Rick and Fred each have been married for a long time, and they are showing signs of restlessness. To revitalize their marriages, their wives grant them one week to do whatever they please, no questions asked. At first, the deal sounds like a dream come true, but as the week marches on, the two friends discover that their expectations are wildly out of sync with reality. (Comedy) - 2011

programme.title: Get Him to the Greek
programme.desc: An ambitious executive at a record company, Aaron Green (Jonah Hill) gets what looks like an easy assignment: He must escort British rock legend Aldous Snow (Russell Brand) to L.A.'s Greek Theatre for the first stop on a lucrative comeback-concert tour. Snow, however, has different plans. Learning his true love is in California, the rocker vows to win her back before starting the tour, forcing Aaron to pull out all the stops to get Snow on stage in time. (Comedy) - 2010

programme.title: Ocean's 11
programme.desc: Danny Ocean (Frank Sinatra) calls on some of his World War II buddies -- including Jimmy Foster (Peter Lawford), Sam Harmon (Dean Martin) and Josh Howard (Sammy Davis Jr.) -- to pull off an elaborate New Year's Eve heist at five casinos in Las Vegas. Eleven members of Danny's crew come together to pull off a perfect robbery, but they suffer a series of setbacks when Duke Santos (Cesar Romero), a former gangster, tries to thwart Ocean's plans to disappear with the money. (Comedy drama) - 1960

programme.title: Ocean's Eleven
programme.desc: Dapper Danny Ocean is a man of action. Less than 24 hours into his parole from a New Jersey penitentiary, the wry, charismatic thief is already rolling out his next plan. Following three rules: Don't hurt anybody, don't steal from anyone who doesn't deserve it, and play the game like you've got nothing to lose. Danny orchestrates the most sophisticated, elaborate casino heist in history. (Comedy drama, Crime drama) - 2001

programme.title: Ocean's Twelve

programme.title: Ocean's Thirteen

programme.desc: Young Alex (Malcolm McDowell) and his droogs commit barbaric acts in a near-future, dehumanizing society. - 1971

programme.desc: After moving from Montana, a youth and his new friends in Florida take on corrupt politicians and greedy developers in a fight to protect endangered owls. - 2006

programme.title: Take the Lead

programme.title: Sweet Dreams
programme.desc: Aspiring country singer Patsy Cline (Jessica Lange) is resigned to both her thankless gigs and her unhappy marriage, until she meets the charismatic Charlie Dick (Ed Harris). Eventually leaving her husband to marry Charlie, Patsy temporarily shelves her performing career to be a mother. Later she returns to singing and finds success under manager Randy Hughes (David Clennon). Patsy hits a remarkable stride with a string of hit singles, and has become a full-fledged star when tragedy strikes. (Biography) - 1985

programme.title: Kiss of the Spider Woman
programme.desc: In a prison cell somewhere in Latin America, two very different men warily confront each other. Molina (William Hurt) is first seen wrapping his head in a towel, in the shape of a turban, while Valentin (Raul Julia), bearded and classically macho in appearance, watches with a mixture of fascination and revulsion. During the time spent together, the two men come to understand and respect each other. (Drama) - 1985

programme.title: Robin Hood
programme.desc: After the death of Richard the Lion-Hearted, a skilled archer named Robin Longstride travels to Nottingham, where villagers suffer under a despotic sheriff and crippling taxation. He meets and falls in love with a spirited widow, Marion, although she is skeptical of his motives. Hoping to win her heart and save the village, Robin gathers a band of warriors to fight corruption in Nottingham, little knowing they will soon be fighting to save England itself. (Adventure, Action, Fantasy, Historical drama) - 2010

programme.title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
programme.desc: Ghost Dog (Forest Whitaker) is a contract killer, a master of his trade who can whirl a gun at warp speed and moves through this world like a phantom -- stealthy and evanescent. In the spirit of the samurai, he has pledged his loyalty to a small time mobster named Louie (John Tormey) who saved his life many years before. (Crime drama) - 1999

programme.title: It
programme.desc: In 1960, seven preteen outcasts fight an evil demon that poses as a child-killing clown. Thirty years later, they reunite to stop the demon once and for all when it returns to their hometown. (Drama, Fantasy, Horror, Mystery, Thriller) - 1990

programme.title: The Hitcher
programme.desc: While transporting a car from Chicago to San Diego, Jim Halsey (C. Thomas Howell) picks up a hitchhiker named John Ryder (Rutger Hauer), who claims to be a serial killer. After a daring escape, Jim hopes to never see Ryder again. But when he witnesses the hitchhiker murdering an entire family, Jim pursues Ryder with the help of truck-stop waitress Nash (Jennifer Jason Leigh), pitting the rivals against each other in a deadly series of car chases and brutal murders. (Thriller) - 1986

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." That's repeated in the second half of the show, and two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. Models present the prizes. (Game show) - 1972-09-04

programme.title: Iron Curtain: Life Under Soviet Occupation
programme.desc: S01 E02 The Reign of Stalin Soviet domination of Eastern European countries will be total and will remain so until the dictator's death in 1953.

programme.title: Africa Freed
programme.desc: A look at the United Nations's conquest of Tunisia, who on land, sea and air, worked as one.

programme.desc: S01 E01 Yom Kippur War - 1973 Arab-Israeli War Yom Kippur, the holiest day on the Jewish calendar; Israeli troops came under surprise attack by Syrian and Egyptian forces, ten times greater than their own.

programme.title: Kwai - The Death Railway
programme.desc: In 1942, Japan forced over 200,000 Asian civilians and 65,000 Western POWs to build a railway through the Thai-Burmese jungle. After 15 months, 120,000 were dead from exhaustion, hunger, and disease.

programme.title: Crusade in the Pacific
programme.desc: S01 E03 The Rise of the Japanese Empire The rise of Japanese power leads to the attack on Pearl Harbor.

programme.title: Architects of Darkness
programme.desc: S02 E03 Karl Doenitz Karl Doenitz, a ruthless Nazi commander, Hitler called him "The Man with the Iron Heart"; he helped design the Holocaust, responsible for the imprisonment, torture and deaths of millions.

programme.title: Hitler and Churchill: The Eagle And the Lion
programme.desc: S01 E01 Winston Churchill, a revered man of the century versus Adolf Hitler, a hated leader in contemporary history.

programme.title: Patton's Finest Hour: The Battle of the Bulge
programme.desc: S01 E03 Tigers on the Loose A combat story of 10th armored division in World War II.

programme.title: The History of Tanks
programme.desc: Documenting the changing face of tank warfare over the past 100 years, this fascinating documentary is not to be missed by those with an interest in military history and weapon development.

programme.title: WWII: Mysteries in the Archives 1938-1948
programme.desc: S01 E10 The Long Trial of Tokyo In 1946, Tokyo, 28 top Japanese officials are tried for war crimes by an international tribunal, modeled on Nuremberg; the trial lasts two and a half years; exploring how did the trial impact Japan and why it took so long.

programme.title: D-Day: The Longest of Days
programme.desc: S01 E18 The Year 1944 Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin congregate at the Teheran Conference in 1943; U.S. troops land and fight on Kwajalein, Eniwetok, Saipan, Guam and other Pacific islands; Russian troops advance to Romania and capture German soldiers.

programme.title: Battlezone: The Gulf War

programme.title: Bomber: Terror of WWII

programme.title: Secrets of the Nazis
programme.desc: S01 E09 Summer On June 22, 1941, Nazi Germany launched Operation Barbarossa, invading the USSR and shattering the non-aggression pact; the Soviets, caught off guard, faced disaster.

programme.title: Guy Martin's D-Day Landing
programme.desc: To mark the 75th anniversary of D-Day, Guy Martin restores a Dakota plane and parachutes into the Normandy countryside where the operation occurred.

programme.title: My Grandparents' War

programme.title: Nazi Death Marches

programme.desc: The ME262, known as one of the best aircraft of World War Two and created by German engineers.

programme.title: Cook's Country
programme.desc: Hosts Bridget Lancaster, Julia Collin Davison and Toni Tipton-Martin offer a practical, no-nonsense and scientific approach to making a wide range of American recipes, from barbecue chicken thighs to Mississippi mud pie to parmesan potatoes. The hosts are joined by test cooks Morgan Bolling, Lawman Johnson, Christie Morrison, Ashley Moore, Bryan Roof and Kelly Song. Episodes include equipment recommendations for the home cook, taste tests and regional recipes such as coastal Georgia paella and mesquite-grilled tacos rasurados. (Cooking) - 2014-08-30

programme.title: My Big Fat Fabulous Life
programme.desc: "My Big Fat Fabulous Life" follows Whitney Thore's emotional journey after being diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome. The disorder caused Whitney, a slender dancer at the time, to gain more than 200 pounds in one year at college. Feeling trapped in a big body, she struggled with self-doubt and negative stereotypes. Now 380 pounds and eager to continue sharing her passion for dance, Whitney has learned to embrace her body and love herself again. She teaches dance classes for plus-size girls, explores the dating scene, confronts bullies, and wears a bikini on the beach for the first time in 10 years. She also spearheads a campaign that fights body-shaming and promotes self-love and acceptance. To that end, Whitney Thore is no longer letting her fear of people's judgment dictate the way she lives her life. (Reality, Documentary, Medical) - 2015-01-13

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World - Labná

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - The Discoveries and Their Significance
programme.desc: Learning about the Dead Sea Scrolls and their discovery; ancient Judaism and early Christianity prior to the scrolls; the uncovering of the scrolls and how they alter one's understanding of every aspect of the historical period of their creation. (Educational, Religious) - 2010-03-05

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - The First Seven Scrolls
programme.desc: Diving into a tale of excitement and adventure and discovering more about how scholars gain access to the first seven scrolls discovered at Qumran; what they find when they begin to translate the extraordinary initial discoveries. (Educational, Religious) - 2010-03-05

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - Opening and Reading the First Scroll
programme.desc: Immersing into the text of the scrolls, starting with the scroll known as the Community Rule or Manual of Discipline; the important text that gives one the first insight into the community and theology of the scrolls' creators and guardians. (Educational, Religious) - 2010-03-05

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - The Historical Backdrop of Ancient Judaism
programme.desc: Examining history prior to the scrolls, beginning with the biblical period and moving to the Maccabean revolt; the arrival of the Romans; King Herod's reign; the life of Jesus; the Zealot revolt; the destruction of Jerusalem and the fall of Masada. (Educational, Religious) - 2010-03-05

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - The Rise of the Jewish Sects

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - The Dead Sea Site of the Qumran Sect

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - The Emergence of the Rabbinic System

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls - A Dead Sea Scroll from Medieval Cairo
programme.desc: Two copies of the Damascus Document are discovered in a Cairo synagogue in the 1890s; although the copies are medieval, the texts are believed to be ancient, a conclusion later confirmed when fragments of the same texts are found at Qumran. (Educational, Religious) - 2010-03-05

programme.desc: The expansion of Islam and how people fared under Muslim rule. (World history) - 2022-04-22

programme.title: The Middle Ages Around the World - Creating an Islamic Culture
programme.desc: The cultural transformations that Muslim rule brought to its domains. (World history) - 2022-04-22

programme.title: The Vikings - The Vikings in Medieval History
programme.desc: Hostile Christian sources demonize the Vikings; Muslim accounts render them exotic; revisionist historians belittle the Norse raids; archeological finds combined with a study of the Norse sagas enrich the understanding of Scandinavia's medieval past. (Educational, History) - 2005-10-03

programme.title: The Vikings - Land and People of Medieval Scandinavia
programme.desc: Scandinavia's landscape shapes its culture; dense forestation leads to close-knit communities; woodworking and sailing are the key means of long-distance travel; harsh winters engender skill in cold-weather commute; the emergence of great halls. (Educational, History) - 2005-10-03

programme.title: The Vikings - Scandinavian Society in the Bronze Age
programme.desc: The physical evidence paints a picture of the Bronze Age in Scandinavia; Viking ancestors trade Arctic goods, amber and slaves in exchange for foreign copper and tin; new wealth fosters larger villages; the beginnings of the Norse pantheon. (Educational, History) - 2005-10-03

programme.title: The Vikings - Scandinavia in the Celtic and Roman Ages
programme.desc: Scandinavia survives on trade with the Celts; contact with Rome enriches the upper classes; Scandinavians returning from Roman military service bring back advanced weapons and armor; petty kings and the first Scandinavian sailing ships emerge. (Educational, History) - 2005-10-03

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World - The Lure of the City
programme.desc: Cities are integral to modern lives; why wandering ancient humans leave the forests and plains to create settlements; the fundamental question of "why" is the first step toward understanding the inhabitants and lessons from ancient cities. (World history) - 2014-08-29

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World - Çatalhöyük - First Experiment in Urban Living
programme.desc: Imagining a city with no streets, public buildings or common spaces; the world's first city offers an intriguing window into life in the Neolithic era; exploring the remains of Çatalhöyük's family housing, murals and religious shrines. (World history) - 2014-08-29

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World - Jericho and Its Walls
programme.desc: The story of the walls of Jericho in the Book of Joshua; looking past the biblical story; what architectural remains suggest about Jericho, whose ritual spaces help create a community and whose walls help define the urban environment.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World - Uruk - City of Gilgamesh
programme.desc: Looking at one of the most marvelous cities in the ancient world; Uruk exhibits many of the hallmarks of ancient civilization; division of labor among its craftsmen; a class hierarchy that includes professional priests; records of art and literature.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation - The World of Late Antiquity
programme.desc: Exploring the origin of the term late antiquity; why this historical view better reflects the period from the third to the eighth centuries than the traditional view that Rome has a decline and fall; the major themes and issues of the course.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation - The Crisis of the 3rd Century
programme.desc: The crisis of the third century, when Rome finds its frontiers threatened on several fronts; armies make and unmake emperors with alarming regularity; the literature of the period also reveals unmistakable feelings of despair and uncertainty.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation - The New Empire of Diocletian
programme.desc: No one predicts that Rome is about to raise two of its greatest rulers, Diocletian and Constantine; Diocletian institutes a series of reforms that divide the empire into east and west; launching the last and fiercest persecution of Christians.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation - Constantine's Roman Revolution
programme.desc: Turning to Constantine; how he extends Diocletian's reforms; among them, he gives the empire a new capital at Byzantium, which he renames Constantinople after himself; he also takes the surprising step of legalizing Christianity.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas - Three Peoples Collide
programme.desc: Neither the Eurocentric term 'discovery' nor the blandly neutral 'encounters' do justice to the impact of Europeans, Africans and Native Americans coming together in the New World; a collision whose causes and effects are outlined in this lecture.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas - The Native Americans
programme.desc: Most of the inhabitants of the Americas arrive in migratory waves from Asia between 40,000 and 2,000 B.C.; their civilizations are based on sophisticated irrigation and farming; complex religions and social structures; rivaling those of Europe.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas - Mayas, Aztecs, and Incas
programme.desc: The Aztecs and Incas create empires built upon religions of conquest; powered by the control of water, around Lake Texcoco in Mexico and high in the Andes Mountains, respectively; the Maya develops an advanced knowledge of astronomy and mathematics.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas - Europeans and Africans
programme.desc: Europe and Africa are connected for centuries by Old World trading networks centered around the Mediterranean; in the 15th century, Spain and Portugal shift the trade out of the Mediterranean and into the Atlantic, along the west coast of Africa.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years - 1990: America's New World Order
programme.desc: The end of the Cold War is a key point in history; the rapid collapse of the Soviet Union; the fall of the Berlin Wall; delving into the American story in the early 1990s; conflicts in Kuwait and Bosnia test America's new role in a post-Soviet world.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years - The Clintons and the 1990s
programme.desc: Bill Clinton's presidency dominates the domestic news in the 1990s. From his dramatic showdown with Newt Gingrich and the Republican Congress's Contract with America, this is a presidency of high drama; surveying the tumultuous decade.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years - A New Millennium, George W. Bush, and 9/11
programme.desc: The end of the Cold War may have reshaped the world order, but 9/11 and the subsequent war on terror changes America; tracing the events leading up to the terrorist attack on American soil on Sept. 11, 2001; learning why 19 hijackers attack America.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years - The US Wars in Afghanistan and Iraq
programme.desc: Historians discuss and debate the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq; the war in Afghanistan has some justification, given the role of Al-Qaeda in 9/11; Professor Allitt reviews the facts surrounding the war in Iraq; the war's effect on the United States.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment - An Overview of Democracy in America
programme.desc: The course begins with a brief overview of Tocqueville's masterwork; written to educate the French about democracy; it is originally published as two separate volumes, released five years apart.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment - Alexis de Tocqueville-A Brief Biography
programme.desc: William R. Cook introduces the young French nobleman, trained as a lawyer; his most famous book is only one achievement in a life marked by several; service as France's foreign minister; a history of the French Revolution regarded as a classic.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment - The Journey to America
programme.desc: Tocqueville rarely describes specific events or conversations; his letters and journals allow one to follow him on his trip; getting an excellent feel for the experiences he and his colleague, Gustave de Beaumont, have in America.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment - Equality of Conditions and Freedom
programme.desc: This lecture considers the meaning and implications of what Tocqueville introduces in the first paragraph of "Democracy in America"; the foundation of the democratic enterprise; the concept he calls equality of conditions.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era - 1865: "Bind Up the Nation's Wounds"
programme.desc: The key historical forces that characterize the Gilded Age and the Progressive Era; the competing ideals that define these eras; the US in 1865; the extraordinary social, political and economic changes unleashed by the devastation of the Civil War.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era - The Reconstruction Revolution
programme.desc: The Reconstruction era following the Civil War; governmental policies and legislation enacted to safeguard the welfare of former slaves and average citizens; these policies are progressively dismantled, the South comes under the rule of the whites.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don conducts a personal grand tour around Italy's magnificent gardens from the luxurious retreats of the moneyed north to the lavish hideaways of the romantic south. In this episode, he's in and around Rome, a powerbase of emperors and popes, to explore gardens that are among some of the most extravagant and flamboyant ever created in history.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don is on a grand tour around Italy, this time visiting gardens both in Florence and around the sun-scorched Tuscan countryside. Monty discovers how, like a piece of sculpture, renaissance gardens were created as works of art, and how a group of Edwardian ex-pats mistakenly reinforced the idea that formal Italian gardens were flowerless.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don continues his grand garden tour of Italy. This time he is in Naples to visit some of the most sublime, romantic retreats in southern Italy. After all the formality of the green gardens around Rome and Florence, Monty seeks out idyllic horticultural gems set against the dramatic scenery of the Amalfi Coast to discover why, in the south, gardens are informal and, above all, filled with flowers.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don concludes his garden tour of Italy in the wealthy north where, in the Veneto and Lucca, extravagant pleasure gardens were created for flirtation and fun. In the Lakes, Monty meets up with the garden society, the Grandi Giardini Italiani, to peer over the fence at luxurious creations of the rich and famous. The journey ends on Lake Maggiore to see the most theatrical horticultural gem of Italy.

programme.title: Monty Don's Paradise Gardens
programme.desc: In Morocco, Monty discovers the wide variety of paradise gardens. He begins just outside the city of Marrakesh in an enormous royal walled meadow, The Agdal. From there he moves to the heart of the town where he comes upon a tiny garden where huge banana plants jostle with palms to create a secret paradise garden, a shelter from the busy world outside. And in another part of the city a rundown old palace has been turned into a stunning contemporary garden with a twist.

programme.title: Monty Don's Paradise Gardens
programme.desc: In Turkey Monty is dazzled by an extraordinary display of the Ottoman Empire's favourite flower, the tulip, and learns of its sacred significance. Travelling further East to India he encounters a new type of spirituality in the tomb gardens of the Mughal Empire. Stunning mausoleums were set in vast gardens as places where an earthly king could enter a divine paradise.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In October 1993, a robber surprised unsuspecting customers by dropping through the roof of a California bank. When police arrived, he escaped from the roof in a hail of bullets. A tip from a local resident led police and FBI agents to the perpetrator. They would soon learn that he had masterminded a local kidnapping, and held the fate of an innocent woman in his hands.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In January 1984, a U.S. Customs official disappears from his post near the Del Rio, Texas border crossing, prompting local police to search for four Latin American suspects driving a Pontiac Grand Prix. The following day, the Customs official was found dead. Two state troopers recovered the missing officer's service revolver after a fatal altercation with two men. Local police and the FBI continued searching for the suspect vehicle, prepared for a confrontation with desperate criminals.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: Amid the cocaine wars of early 1980's Miami, three dead bodies led a multi-agency tactical squad to suspect that a group of cops might be involved in illegal drug busts. Investigating rumors of corruption, the squad uncovered a ring of patrolmen who were making millions by ripping off smuggled cocaine. The investigators set out to prove that even with the advantages wealth and the protection of a police badge, nobody is above the law.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: At 9:30 am on the morning of January 30, 1997, Richmond, VA police respond to a report of shots fired at a local bank. Two masked men brandishing automatic weapons confront, and open fire on officers responding to the call. The gunmen exit the bank, and retreat on foot, eventually eluding the officers. The FBI soon responds, only to find one bank teller dead, another wounded, and the bank's security guard shot four times, yet still alive.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: A man is found suffocated in his Pennsylvania home, his checkbook, credit cards and vehicle appear to have been stolen. Fingerprints from the victim identify a recent escapee from a minimum-security prison, as well as his girlfriend. Investigators flag the dead man's credit cards, and are alerted when one is used in North Dakota. The FBI is called in and joins another task force already assembled because of a suspected kidnapping.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In Wisconsin, a varsity athlete is blindfolded, gagged, and shoved into a van by four gunmen. The kidnappers contact the victim's family and demand $30,000, but offer no instructions on how to transfer the money. The victim's family contacts the police. The boy's captors tell his family they have shot him, and will kill him if they do not receive their money. At an agreed upon drop site, FBI agents approach the captor's vehicle, only to watch them flee and quickly be followed by authorities.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: A New Jersey State Trooper is shot to death on the side of Interstate 80 near the Pennsylvania border. Witnesses to the shooting identify the shooter's car. Police issue an APB, and locate the vehicle hours later. Fingerprinting of the vehicle points to a fugitive wanted on bank robbery charges. Authorities who inspect the fugitive's home find some incriminating evidence including a box of bullets linked to the Trooper's murder.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In 1991, the Safe Streets Task Force, a joint FBI / Washington D.C. Metropolitan Police Department organization, begins conducting an investigation into the violent activities of a local gang called the K Street Crew. Gang members are suspected of involvement in several area homicides. The FBI approaches several witnesses, hoping to convince them to testify against the gang members. Seven potential witnesses are murdered during the course of the investigation.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In June of 2000, two gunmen rob a Seattle, WA bank, and flee on foot as officers chase them. One of the gunmen is killed in a firefight with police, the other escapes after assaulting a family and using their home to hide. The family helps FBI agents identify the man, who is suspected of several other robberies. Seattle SWAT teams, working with the FBI, search the home of the assailant's mother, and find ammunition matching that used at the bank robbery.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: A California bank manager panics and calls in the FBI after the door to his vault refuses to open. Upon inspection, the vault has been blasted into from the ceiling, and over $2 million in valuables is gone. When agents find no clues as to the robbers or their whereabouts in California, they send details of the crime to other FBI field offices. It is not long before agents in Ohio are investigating a bank vault robbery that is strikingly similar to the California heist.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: An Arkansas State Trooper is shot and killed after pulling over a van for a traffic violation. Officers apprehend the shooter, after a car chase and shootout. ATF is alerted when officers find weapons and explosives in the man's vehicle. Further testing of the weapons reveals one was used in a murder several months earlier. ATF traces some of the firearms to purchases made by another man from and arms dealer. They also match silencer marks from the weapons to a third man previously arrested for stealing a flatbed truck.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: A Washington DC professor is shot and killed as she tries to get into her car. The killer leaves the body in the parking lot and drives away in her vehicle. A week later, a man robs a bank, and security cameras capture the same vehicle as the getaway car. The FBI believes they are dealing with the same man. Days later, the same vehicle is involved in a shootout with police, but eventually would elude them. Eventually, the vehicle is found, the interior covered with red dye from the stolen bank packs.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: Four inmates from a Delaware Correctional Center turn up missing in the middle of the night. A few hours later, a stolen vehicle is recovered; inside, one of the inmate's fingerprints is found, as well as the address book of one of the other fugitives. A multi-state manhunt ensues with the help of the FBI. A nearby robbery report is the agent's first tip, followed by a murder in the same neighborhood.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In the Spring of 1997, a killer preying on senior citizens terrorizes the River Parish area of Southern Louisiana. By May, local police and the New Orleans FBI are exploring a connection between the April 9 murder of a 71-year old widow and the May 9 murder of a retired couple. A month later, authorities forward information on the crimes to the FBI's Behavioral Science Unit in Quantico, VA, hoping a profile will help them narrow the field of possible suspects.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: On December 21, 1998, two gunmen kidnap three janitors on their way to clean the Bank of America ATM repository in Las Vegas. The gunmen force the janitors to let them in the ATM repository and hold them hostage until the armored car guards arrive to make their nightly collection. When the guards enter the bank, the gunmen surprise them and shoot one guard in the chest before escaping with $1,088,000, the largest bank robbery take in Las Vegas history.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In Henderson, NV, a suburb of Las Vegas, two robbers brandishing assault rifles ambush armored guards as they exit their truck on March 3, 2000. The robbers kill both guards and seize $5,000. As the killers run to their getaway car, a police officer arrives and opens fire, striking one escaping assailant in the leg. After loosing the killers in a chase, police collect blood left by the injured robber and bullet casings from the firefight.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: On February 12, 1997, two men use a sledgehammer to break into a Camden, NJ home. The homeowner shoots at the intruders, hitting one in the hand before they escape. Camden Police respond and track the suspects to a nearby park. One of the men shoots at the officer before police arrest his accomplice. The man gives up the identity of the shooter. Twice, police stake out homes where they believe the shooter is hiding, but he eludes them.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: When violent criminals strike, the FBI strikes back, employing every available resource, and creating new ones when necessary. From forensic science to criminal profiling, specialized intelligence to global fugitive tracking, the agents of the FBI battle the bad guys with a most powerful arsenal: the crime-fighter's toolbox. This special episode of The FBI Files celebrates the groundbreaking science, investigative technique, and gut-level instinct that has made the FBI the world's premier law enforcement agency.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In the 1970's, Otpor, a violent arm of the Croatian National Resistance commits terroristic acts against non-supportive Croatians living in the U.S. With the help of an informant, the FBI is able to apprehend, arrest and convict members of the group for crimes ranging from conspiracy and extortion to murder.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In 1994, a rash of home invasion robberies take place in the metropolitan Detroit area. The thieves turn out to be part of a local gang dubbed the Home Invaders. Their crimes extend to insurance fraud, theft, and illegal lottery schemes. The Violent Crimes Task Force (VCTF) opens an investigation, and with the cooperation of a gang member who was apprehended at the scene of a crime, they are able to obtain the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of 16 gang members.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: This is the story of the FBI's first capture of an international Lebanese terrorist. In June 1985, the terrorist and his four accomplices hijacked Royal Jordanian flight #405 shortly before take off in Beirut, Lebanon. On board were American citizens, a professor and his teen son. The FBI opened a criminal investigation and worked with various other government agencies to form Operation Goldenrod, a task force specifically charged with bringing the terrorist to justice in 1989.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In the late 1970s, the FBI had a working knowledge of anti-Castro terrorists operating in the United States. But then a new group appeared, more violent and aggressive than their predecessors. All agents had to go on was a series of chilling phone calls, a mysterious voice, and the threat of more violence. FBI field offices from New York to Miami coordinated their efforts, determined to catch the vicious killers.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In the late 70s and early 80s, a terrorist group known as the FALN is suspected of setting off bombs in major U.S. cities. Their goal - to bring attention to the Puerto Rican independence movement. As the bombings escalate, innocent lives are lost. FBI agents and police are is in a deadly race to stop this murderous group with a dangerous cause.
